ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: In 711 Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed from North Africa and defeated King Roderic; within a few years most of the peninsula was under Umayyad rule.
Founded in 756 by Abd al-Rahman I, a survivor of the Abbasid massacre of his family, it made al-Andalus an independent Islamic state.
Begun in 785 and enlarged by later emirs and caliphs, its forest of double-arched columns became a cathedral after the Christian conquest of 1236.
Christians who lived under Muslim rule and adopted Arabic language and culture while keeping their faith and their own liturgy.
Abd al-Rahman III's caliphate of 929 made Córdoba the largest city of western Europe, with the palace city of Madinat al-Zahra and celebrated libraries.
When the caliphate broke apart, rival taifa kings paid tribute to Christian rulers, until the fall of Toledo in 1085 brought in the Almoravids.
Philosopher, physician and judge to the Almohad caliphs, whose commentaries on Aristotle, translated into Latin, shaped European scholasticism.
Born in Córdoba, he left al-Andalus with his family under Almohad pressure, settled in Egypt and became one of medieval Judaism's most influential thinkers.
The last Muslim state in Iberia survived as a tributary of Castile for over 250 years, built the Alhambra and surrendered on 2 January 1492.
